subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.

questions.q: Alkenes are described as unsaturated because they contain:
questions.explain: Alkenes are unsaturated because they contain at least one C=C double bond.

questions.q: Silicon dioxide is an example of a:
questions.explain: Silicon dioxide has a giant covalent (macromolecular) structure.

questions.q: Why is cracking carried out on some crude oil fractions?
options: There is too little demand for short-chain hydrocarbons
Demand for short-chain fractions like petrol is greater than supply
questions.explain: Cracking matches supply to demand, as there is more demand for short-chain hydrocarbons than the supply from crude oil.

questions.q: Why do simple molecular substances have low melting and boiling points?
questions.explain: Only weak intermolecular forces need to be overcome, not the strong covalent bonds.
Electrons are transferred from the metal atom to the non-metal atom, forming ions.

questions.q: Why do ionic compounds have high melting points?
options: They are made of free electrons
Strong electrostatic forces throughout a giant lattice
questions.explain: Strong electrostatic attractions in the giant ionic lattice need lots of energy to break.

questions.q: A covalent bond is formed when atoms:
questions.explain: Covalent bonds form when non-metal atoms share pairs of electrons.

questions.q: During incomplete combustion of a hydrocarbon, which products may form?
options: Carbon monoxide and/or carbon (soot), and water
questions.explain: Incomplete combustion in limited oxygen can produce carbon monoxide and/or carbon as well as water.

questions.q: The complete combustion of a hydrocarbon produces:
questions.explain: Complete combustion of a hydrocarbon produces carbon dioxide and water.

questions.q: What is the general formula of the alkenes?
questions.explain: Alkenes have the general formula CnH2n.

Each carbon bonds to four others
questions.explain: In graphite each carbon bonds to three others, leaving delocalised electrons that carry charge.

questions.q: What is observed when an alkene is shaken with orange bromine water?
questions.explain: Alkenes decolourise bromine water because the C=C double bond reacts with the bromine.
